newsitem.title: USA: Angeion gets European approval for ICDs.
newsitem.headline: Angeion gets European approval for ICDs.

text.p: Angeion Corp said it received Conformite Europeene Mark approval for its Sentinel 2011 and 2012 implantable cardioverter defibrillator systems.
The CE Mark allows Angeion to market the Sentinel 2011 and 2012 ICDs in the European Union, the company said.
In addition to the Sentinel 2011 and 2012, the CE Mark includes Angeion's Model 3007 programmer, Model 3008 printer and Model 5020 patient cable.
The 2011 and 2012 models complete Angeion's Sentinel 2010 Series of ICDs. In 1996, Angeion received CE Mark approvals on the Sentinel 2000 and 2010 ICD systems.
ICDs are small electronic devices implanted in the body and wired to the heart to keep it from beating too fast.

Last month, Angeion received U.S. Food and Drug Administration permission to expand its U.S. clinical studies of the Sentinel 2000 and 2010 ICD systems and to add Models 2011 and 2012 to the U.S. clinical evaluations.
